title: tinyfloat-collapse-scratchpad
body:
Goal: rapid notes + breadcrumbs for a weird "tinyfloat collapse" phenomenon seen when running inference with mixed INT8 + FP8 kernels. Trying to capture reproducible steps, observed artifacts, quick checks, and mitigation ideas so we (me + Ethan/Maya) can triage faster.

High-level symptom:
- Long-context generation (>2048 tokens) occasionally devolves into repeating token loops or produces NaNs in the KV cache.
- Happens more often when model is served with INT8 matmul kernels + FP8 activations (experimental path) or when enabling Aggressive KV caching optimizations.
- Not deterministic: appears after many tokens (sequence-dependent), and sometimes after warmup/priming prompts.

Immediate context / environment:
- Model: open-llama-13b-v2-like (attention + rotary), converted to Redwood-optimized graph.
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.12.4 (local dev image) with fallback to reference kernels.
- Hardware: A100-80GB (driver 525) and M60-ng testbed (emulated lower-precision).
- Config used in failing runs: quant_scheme: {"matmul":"int8", "weights_layout":"Q4_0", "activations":"fp8_e4m3"}, kv_cache_opt: "aggressive", batch_size:1, max_seq:8192.

Repro quick-check (minimal harness I ran):
- script: tests/repro/tinyfloat_collapse_minimal.py (attached in PR draft)
- invocation: "python tinyfloat_collapse_minimal.py --model models/13b/optim-graph --quant int8-fp8 --max-tokens 4096"
- observed stdout snippets: "step 312: attn_out max_abs=1.2e4" then "step 319: attn_out max_abs=nan count=472" then generator loops: "<bos> <bos> <bos> ..."

Commands tried (notes inline):
1) Re-run with FP32 matmul kernel fallback:
   export RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREF=fp32
   ./run_infer.sh --quant int8-fp8
   -> result: no NaNs observed in 5/5 runs. Suggests int8 matmul interacts with fp8 activations.

2) Disable aggressive KV caching:
   config: kv_cache_opt: none
   -> result: reduces frequency but does not eliminate (2/5 runs still fail).

3) Inject small activation clipping after attention (hack):
   clip(attn_out, -1e3, +1e3) before writeback to KV cache.
   -> result: prevents NaNs for tested traces but causes slight degradation on perplexity (~0.6% relative).
   -> suggests runaway dynamic range in attention outputs.

4) Instrument per-layer max abs in KV cache:
   quick profiler logs: layer_7.kv_max_abs=3.2e5 at t=318, layer_8.kv_max_abs=NaN after t=319.
   -> pattern: often a single layer explodes then contaminates subsequent layers.

Error snippets / stack traces (copied as-is):
- Runtime log: "ERROR: mem_write: attempted write NaN to kv_cache shard=0 layer=8 offset=0x17c3"
- Traceback (cleaned): RuntimeError: kernel_matmul_int8: output contains NaN (detected by sanity check)
    at serving_runtime/kernels/int8_matmul.cu:142
    at runtime/executor.cc:893

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
- H1: INT8 matmul quantization scales are getting stale for long contexts; scale underflow/overflow leads to amplification when combined with FP8 exponent bias.
- H2: Mixed-precision path has mismatched rounding semantics between matmul and subsequent cast-to-fp8, producing subnormal/inf values that propagate into KV cache.
- H3: Aggressive KV cache memory layout reuses buffers causing stale metadata (scale/zero-point) to be applied to wrong tensors (indexing bug).
- H4: Rotary embedding or relative pos encoding applied post-quantization causes periodic amplification (phase drift).

Quick unit experiments to differentiate hypotheses:
- To test H1: Run static per-op recalibration every 256 steps (recompute scale from sample minibatch) and observe. I tried recalibration with a sliding-window and failure rate dropped from 40% -> 5% in local runs.
- To test H2: Replace the FP8 cast with an explicit fp32->fp16->fp8 path (simulate different rounding). Failure unaffected. That points away from naive rounding mismatch.
- To test H3: Add guard tags to KV buffer headers (inc 64-bit sentinel) and assert on reads. After adding sentinel checks, failed runs triggered header mismatch at t=319 once. That is a strong signal for memory corruption or misindexing.
- To test H4: Bypassing rotary embeddings (use absolute pos) removed the collapse in one reproducible run but not all. Mixed result.

Notes on numeric diagnostics I captured:
- per-token distribution stats (example):
  t=318: attn_softmax_mean=0.0032, attn_softmax_std=0.14, attn_out_max=3.2e5, attn_out_min=-2.1e5
  t=319: attn_softmax_mean=NaN, attn_out_max=NaN, kv_shard0_nan_count=472
- memory pattern: KV write addresses clustered around 0x1c00-0x1d00 for layers 7-9, repeats every 64 tokens -> suggests stride mismatch with block_size=64.

Immediate mitigations tested (temporary):
- Add NaN guard before KV write: if any(isnan(tensor)) -> skip write + mark fallback to fp32. This keeps the convo live but loses some context; acceptable as emergency mitigation for hosted API.
- Periodic format-safe checkpoint: every 256 tokens, flush and re-encode KV cache in fp32. This alleviates but costs ~12% throughput.

Actionable next steps (prioritized):
1) Reproduce with deterministic seed on both HW variants (A100 and M60 emulation). Log buffer addresses + headers to see pointer arithmetic mismatch. (Owner: Sofia)
2) Run sanitizer build with bounds checks for KV index computations; reproduce at scale with longer sequences. (Owner: Ethan)
3) Add more granular sentinel headers to kv cache (per-shard per-layer) and fail fast with diagnostic dump. (Owner: Maya)
4) If H3 confirmed, audit memcpy/strided-write code paths between optimized matmul and kv writer for block_size assumptions. (Owner: eng-platform)
5) Draft a short runbook for Hosted fallback: auto-disable int8 path if sentinel mismatch detected. (Owner: product-ops)

Misc notes / oddities:
- I saw one run where only odd-numbered layers exploded; another where layers 0..3 were fine then a single middle layer poisoned everything. No clear layer-level deterministic pattern yet.
- The failure sometimes correlates with a particular input token (rare tokens that trigger high-attention spike) — possibly a rare-word amplification bug.
- Logged a crash dump to s3: s3://redwood-debug/tinyfloat-collapse/2025-11-03-run12/ (contains tensor snapshots, kernel args).

Short-term experiment plan (this week):
- [ ] Add boundary-sanitizer build and run overnight on A100 with seed matrix (5 seeds x 3 prompt types).
- [ ] Add KV sentinel + auto-snapshot on mismatch (low-cost, should be safe to ship to dev cluster).
- [ ] Try disabling Q4_0 layout to Q8 variants (different blocking) to see whether block-size interacts with stride mismatch.

Open questions to discuss in sync:
- How aggressive is product comfortable with auto-fallback (throughput penalty) on hosted?
- Any historical changes around block_size 64 -> 128 that could have introduced an off-by-factor bug? (release notes point to a patch in v1.11.2 changing kernel tile size)
- Could FP8 exp range be saturating for certain attention kernels - do we have monitoring for fp8 exponent overflow counts?

Notes-to-self: keep this doc alive as timeline of experiments. If we confirm H3 (indexing/mem corruption), prioritize backport with high urgency. If it's pure numeric instability, lean on clipping + periodic re-encode.

End of scratchpad.

Latest snapshot attachments (local): tests/repro/tinyfloat_collapse_minimal.py, scripts/kv_sentinel_injector.sh, perf/logs/2025-11-03-run12-tensors.tar.gz

If anyone reading: please ping me on Slack (#eng-applied-ml) with any extra bits — I probably left half the intermediate logs on my laptop.
